buildTools.technical.title: Full technical explanation
buildTools.technical.shell.title: Shell choices
buildTools.technical.shell.text: ucrt64 is the recommended modern Windows build environment. mingw64 is the traditional MinGW-w64 environment. clang64 uses Clang/LLVM.
buildTools.technical.packages.title: Package list

buildTools.technical.scope.title: What belongs here
buildTools.technical.scope.text: This list is only for build tools such as compilers, make, pkg-config, CMake, Ninja, NASM, and YASM. Codec libraries are selected in the FFmpeg Libraries tab.

libraries.intro: Choose a starting preset, then adjust individual libraries if needed.
libraries.info.builtIn: Built-in FFmpeg parts are already included.
libraries.info.external: External libraries add extra features, packages, and possible license requirements.
libraries.presetSelector.title: Library preset
libraries.presetSelector.text: Choose a starting point. You can still check or uncheck individual libraries after applying a preset.
libraries.presetSelector.custom: Custom selection. The checked libraries no longer match one preset exactly.
libraries.presets.custom.name: Custom
libraries.technical.title: Full technical explanation
libraries.technical.builtIn.title: Built-in parts
libraries.technical.builtIn.text: Locked checked rows mean included by the normal FFmpeg source build. They are shown so the page does not look empty when no extra external library is selected.
libraries.technical.external.title: External libraries
libraries.technical.external.text: External libraries are not used by FFmpeg by default. Selecting one can add packages, configure flags, and license requirements.
libraries.technical.configure.title: Configure flags and packages
libraries.technical.configure.text: Official FFmpeg documentation says native decoders and encoders are enabled by default, while decoders and encoders requiring external libraries must be enabled manually with a matching --enable-lib... option.
libraries.technical.license.title: License boundary
libraries.technical.license.text: The app derives the license boundary from selected libraries. GPL libraries require a GPL build. Nonfree libraries require a nonfree local build.
libraries.presets.minimal.name: Minimal
libraries.presets.minimal.plain: Bare FFmpeg source build with only the programs and libraries included by a plain ./configure run.
libraries.presets.minimal.technical: No external codec or multimedia package is added. This is what you get from a plain FFmpeg source compile without extra --enable-lib flags.
libraries.presets.default.name: Default
libraries.presets.default.plain: Matches what widely distributed Windows FFmpeg builds ship: GPU hardware encoding plus the common codec, audio, subtitle, and protocol libraries.
libraries.presets.default.technical: Includes hardware encoders (NVENC, AMF, QSV), major video codecs (H.264, H.265, VP9, AV1, Theora, Xvid), common audio codecs, subtitle rendering, stabilization, and standard protocol support. Matches the gyan.dev release-essentials build profile.
libraries.presets.efficiency.name: Maximum Efficiency
libraries.presets.efficiency.plain: Default plus high-quality AAC encoding and audio resampling.
libraries.presets.efficiency.technical: Includes everything in Default plus FDK AAC (best AAC encoder) and SoX high-quality resampler. The preset follows feature goals first; the derived license boundary is shown later in Build FFmpeg.
libraries.presets.compatibility.name: Maximum Compatibility
libraries.presets.compatibility.plain: Default plus broader codec coverage so the build can open or create more media formats.
libraries.presets.compatibility.technica: Includes everything in Default plus extra AV1 (rav1e) and H.264 (OpenH264) encoders, iLBC and TwoLAME audio, SoX resampling, EVC decoding (xevd), Codec 2 and LC3 speech, the Shine MP3 encoder, JPEG XS, SVG input, Snappy for HAP, teletext and ARIB caption decoding, and RTMP streaming. The preset follows compatibility first; the derived license boundary is shown later in Build FFmpeg.
libraries.presets.editor.name: Audio/Video Editor
libraries.presets.editor.plain: Default plus editing, filtering, subtitle, image-workflow, and quality-check tools.
libraries.presets.editor.technical: Includes everything in Compatibility plus JPEG XL, PNG, libplacebo GPU processing with Vulkan shader compilation (shaderc), frei0r effects, XML parsing, lcms2 image/color correction, SOFA (mysofa) and bs2b binaural audio, LADSPA and LV2 audio plugin hosting, Chromaprint fingerprinting, QR generation, and whisper speech-to-text. The preset follows editor usefulness first; the derived license boundary is shown later in Build FFmpeg.
libraries.presets.full.name: Full
libraries.presets.full.plain: Selects the broadest set this app can plan without selecting mutually exclusive or known configure-failing alternatives together.
libraries.presets.full.technical: Includes everything in Editor plus Blu-ray/DVD/CD input, module audio, OpenSSL TLS, RIST/RabbitMQ streaming or messaging, Tesseract OCR, JACK/PulseAudio, OpenCL GPU acceleration, and libcaca output. GnuTLS is left unchecked because FFmpeg cannot enable GnuTLS and OpenSSL at the same time.
options.title: FFmpeg Options
options.intro: Choose the general build settings that will be combined with the selected libraries.
options.info.controls: This page controls how FFmpeg is built after the source and libraries are chosen.
options.info.defaults: Use the defaults for a first build. Change license boundary only when the selected libraries require it, and leave advanced flags empty unless a needed option is missing from the checkboxes.
options.license.label: License boundary
options.license.hint: License is determined automatically by the libraries you select. It cannot be set manually, so an LGPL-only build cannot accidentally include a GPL or nonfree library.
options.licenseBoundary.gpl: GPL local - required by selected GPL libraries
options.licenseBoundary.nonfree: Nonfree local - required by selected nonfree items
options.licenseBoundary.lgpl: LGPL local - current selected libraries do not require GPL/nonfree
options.jobs.label: Build jobs
options.jobs.hint: How many compile jobs may run at the same time. Higher is faster but uses more CPU and memory. Use 1 for the safest behavior, or your CPU core count minus one for speed.
options.configure.defaultBehavior: Default FFmpeg behavior; no extra flag is added.
options.presetSelector.title: Option presets
options.presetSelector.text: Pick a starting point for build options. You can still toggle anything below.
options.presetSelector.custom: Custom selection — your options don't match a preset.
options.presets.none.name: None
options.presets.none.plain: No extra build options — plain FFmpeg defaults.
options.presets.standard.name: Standard
options.presets.standard.plain: Recommended. Links external libraries statically and skips documentation.
options.presets.compact.name: Compact
options.presets.compact.plain: Standard plus removing debug data for a smaller release binary.
options.presets.portable.name: Portable
options.presets.portable.plain: Compact plus run-time CPU detection so one build runs on any processor.
options.presets.performance.name: Performance
options.presets.performance.plain: Compact plus link-time optimization, tuned for this machine.
options.advancedFlags.label: Advanced FFmpeg configure flags
options.advancedFlags.hint.prefix: Optional escape hatch. Leave empty unless a needed FFmpeg configure flag is missing from the checkboxes above. One
options.advancedFlags.hint.suffix: flag per line. Review will show every manual flag before backend confirmation.
options.technical.title: Full technical explanation
options.technical.license.title: License boundary
options.technical.configure.title: Configure options
options.technical.configure.text: Each checkbox maps to a single ./configure switch. Checked options add their flag to the build; unchecked options leave FFmpeg's default behavior untouched. Native decoders and encoders are already enabled by default, so these options only toggle build-wide behavior, not individual codecs.
options.technical.advanced.title: Advanced configure flags
options.technical.advanced.text: The advanced flags box is an escape hatch for switches not covered by the checkboxes above. One flag per line. Every manual flag is shown in the build plan for backend confirmation before anything runs.

about.title: About
about.intro: A simple summary of what this app does and how it keeps the build under your control.
about.version.label: Current version
about.technical.title: Full technical explanation
about.does.title: What this app does
about.does.p1: Promptful Custom FFmpeg Builder helps you build FFmpeg on your own Windows computer.
about.does.p2: You choose a workspace folder, pick the libraries and options you want, review the plan, and approve it before anything runs.
about.does.p3: When the build finishes, the app puts the finished FFmpeg files and a build report in the result folder.
about.flow.workspace.label: Choose workspace
about.flow.workspace.caption: Pick where the private build files will live.
about.flow.configure.label: Select build
about.flow.configure.caption: Choose libraries, options, and build tools.
about.flow.review.label: Review and approve
about.flow.review.caption: Check the plan before any action runs.
about.flow.result.label: Get result
about.flow.result.caption: Find FFmpeg files and the build report together.
about.doesNotInclude.title: What this app does not include
about.doesNotInclude.p1: The app does not come with FFmpeg already built.
about.doesNotInclude.p2: It does not include FFmpeg source code, codec libraries, build packages, or hidden build output. Build files are downloaded only after you review and approve the plan.
about.approval.title: How approval works
about.approval.p1: Before a download, extraction, install, build command, or workspace deletion runs, the app shows you what it plans to do.
about.approval.p2: The backend checks that the approved plan is still the same plan. Then it opens a normal system confirmation dialog. The action runs only if you approve that dialog.
about.approval.p3.prefix: The app keeps security events in the Logs tab and in the workspace
about.downloads.title: How downloads are checked
about.downloads.p1: The app uses HTTPS downloads from the allowed official hosts.
about.downloads.p2.prefix: MSYS2 archives are checked with their matching
about.downloads.p2.middle: signature. FFmpeg source archives are checked with their matching
about.downloads.p2.suffix: signature. SHA-256 hashes are also recorded in the logs and build report.
about.downloads.p3: Archives are unpacked only inside the workspace. Unsafe archive entries, such as paths that try to escape the workspace or links from downloaded archives, are blocked.
about.license.title: FFmpeg license
about.license.p1: The license for your build depends on the libraries you choose.
about.license.p2: Built-in FFmpeg parts usually keep the build in the LGPL boundary. GPL libraries make the build GPL. Nonfree libraries make the build nonfree. The FFmpeg Options page shows the current license boundary before you build.
about.license.p3: This app does not give legal advice. Check the FFmpeg license information and the licenses for the libraries you select before sharing a build.
source.archiveUrl.label: Archive URL
source.msys2.technical.archive.title: Archive requirements
source.msys2.technical.archive.text: Use a portable MSYS2 archive. .tar.zst is recommended, and .tar.xz is accepted as a fallback. Do not use .exe or .sfx.exe files here. Those are official MSYS2 installer or self-extractor formats, but this app intentionally does not run installers.
source.msys2.technical.signature.title: Signature verification
source.msys2.technical.signature.text: Use the matching .sig URL for the MSYS2 archive. The app downloads the MSYS2 public signing key, checks its fingerprint, and verifies the archive internally. You do not need to install GPG manually. A .sig file is not readable text, so paste the URL to the .sig file, not the contents of the file.
source.msys2.technical.sha.title: Optional SHA-256 audit check
source.msys2.technical.sha.text: SHA-256 is optional. The app calculates and logs the SHA-256 after download. Use the .sig signature as the authenticity check; use SHA-256 only as an extra audit value when you already have a trusted hash.
source.ffmpeg.technical.archive.title: Archive requirements
source.ffmpeg.technical.archive.text: Use an official FFmpeg source archive, such as ffmpeg-8.1.tar.xz. Use the source-code release, not a prebuilt Windows executable package.
source.ffmpeg.technical.signature.title: Signature verification
source.ffmpeg.technical.signature.text: FFmpeg publishes release archives with matching .asc PGP signatures. Use the .asc URL for authenticity. Do not paste the PGP signature text into this field; paste the URL to the .asc file.
source.ffmpeg.technical.sha.title: Optional SHA-256 audit check
source.ffmpeg.technical.sha.text: Official FFmpeg releases are normally verified with the .asc signature. Leave SHA-256 empty unless you already have a trusted 64-character SHA-256 value from another trusted source.
source.msys2Signature.hint: Use the matching .sig file. The app downloads the MSYS2 public signing key, checks its fingerprint, and verifies the archive internally. You do not need to install GPG manually. A .sig file is not readable text; do not paste its file contents into this field; paste the URL to the .sig file.
source.ffmpegSignature.hint: Use the matching .asc file, for example ffmpeg-8.1.tar.xz.asc. Do not paste the PGP signature text into this field.
source.ffmpegSha.hint: Official FFmpeg releases are normally verified with the .asc signature above. Leave this empty unless you already have a trusted 64-character SHA-256 from another trusted source.
catalog.libraries.amf.plainExplanation: AMF adds AMD graphics-card encoding (GPU encoding), and people choose it because it gives faster video encoding on AMD systems.
catalog.libraries.amf.reviewNote: Enables AMD GPU video encoding (h264_amf, hevc_amf, av1_amf). AMF headers are bundled in FFmpeg source; no extra MSYS2 package is needed. Requires a compatible AMD GPU and driver.
catalog.libraries.amf.technicalExplanati: Check this when you need AMD GPU-accelerated video encoding (h264_amf, hevc_amf, av1_amf). It is not default because it requires a compatible AMD GPU and driver.
catalog.libraries.aom.plainExplanation: AOM adds AV1 video encoding, and people often choose it when they want strong AV1 quality even if encoding takes longer.
catalog.libraries.aom.technicalExplanati: Check this when you need standards-focused AV1 encoding/decoding through libaom. It is not default because AV1 encoding is slow and many users do not need to create AV1 files.
catalog.libraries.aribb24.plainExplanati: libaribb24 adds ARIB B24 caption support, and people choose it for older Japanese broadcast subtitle workflows.
catalog.libraries.aribb24.reviewNote: Adds Japanese ARIB STD-B24 caption decoding. Requires FFmpeg's version-3 license switch.
catalog.libraries.aribb24.technicalExpla: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.aribcaption.plainExpla: libaribcaption adds Japanese broadcast caption support, and people choose it to read captions from Japanese TV sources.
catalog.libraries.aribcaption.reviewNote: Adds an alternative ARIB STD-B24 caption decoder/renderer with richer styling.
catalog.libraries.aribcaption.technicalE: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.ass.plainExplanation: libass adds styled subtitle rendering, and people choose it because it supports fonts, colors, positions, and subtitle effects.
catalog.libraries.ass.technicalExplanati: Check this when you need styled ASS/SSA subtitle rendering, common for fansubs and complex subtitles. It is not default because simple subtitle copy/conversion may not need rendered subtitles.
catalog.libraries.bluray.plainExplanatio: libbluray adds Blu-ray input support, and people choose it to inspect or convert Blu-ray media.
catalog.libraries.bluray.technicalExplan: Check this when you need to read Blu-ray structures. It is not default because many users work with ordinary files rather than disc layouts.
catalog.libraries.bs2b.plainExplanation: bs2b adds headphone crossfeed, and people choose it because it can make headphone listening feel more like speakers.
catalog.libraries.bs2b.reviewNote: Adds Bauer stereophonic-to-binaural processing for more natural headphone listening.
catalog.libraries.bs2b.technicalExplanat: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.caca.plainExplanation: libcaca adds text-mode video output (ASCII art), and people choose it for special visual experiments rather than normal encoding.
catalog.libraries.caca.reviewNote: Adds colored ASCII-art video output through the caca output device.
catalog.libraries.caca.technicalExplanat: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.cdio.plainExplanation: libcdio adds CD input support, and people choose it for audio CD or disc-based input workflows. (Makes the build GPL.)
catalog.libraries.cdio.reviewNote: Adds CD input support. GPL effect.
catalog.libraries.cdio.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need direct CD input support. It is not default because CD input is uncommon and it changes the resulting build to GPL.
catalog.libraries.chromaprint.plainExpla: Chromaprint adds audio fingerprinting, and people choose it to create audio IDs for matching or identifying tracks.
catalog.libraries.chromaprint.reviewNote: Adds audio fingerprinting used for acoustic identification.
catalog.libraries.chromaprint.technicalE: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.codec2.plainExplanatio: Codec 2 adds very low-bitrate speech audio support, and people usually choose it for radio or communication experiments.
catalog.libraries.codec2.reviewNote: Adds Codec 2 very-low-bitrate speech encoding and decoding.
catalog.libraries.codec2.technicalExplan: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.dav1d.plainExplanation: dav1d adds AV1 video decoding, and people choose it because it reads AV1 video quickly and smoothly.
catalog.libraries.dav1d.technicalExplana: Check this when you need fast AV1 playback/decoding. It is not default because native FFmpeg can still be built without it, and users who do not decode AV1 do not need the extra package.
catalog.libraries.fdk-aac.plainExplanati: Fraunhofer FDK AAC adds AAC audio encoding, and people choose it because it gives high-quality AAC for MP4, phones, and web playback. (Makes the build nonfree.)
catalog.libraries.fdk-aac.reviewNote: Adds a high-quality AAC encoder. Makes the FFmpeg build nonfree.
catalog.libraries.fdk-aac.technicalExpla: Check this when you specifically need the Fraunhofer AAC encoder. It is not default because it makes the resulting FFmpeg build nonfree and limits redistribution.
catalog.libraries.ffmpeg-program.plainEx: The main command-line program users normally run.
catalog.libraries.ffmpeg-program.reviewN: The main command-line program users normally run.
catalog.libraries.ffmpeg-program.technic: Built by default in a normal FFmpeg source build. No external package or --enable-lib flag is needed. Only disabled by selecting --disable-programs.
catalog.libraries.ffprobe-program.plainE: The media inspection tool used to check files and streams.
catalog.libraries.ffprobe-program.review: The media inspection tool used to check files and streams.
catalog.libraries.ffprobe-program.techni: Built by default in a normal FFmpeg source build. No external package or --enable-lib flag is needed. Disabled by selecting --disable-programs or --disable-ffprobe.
catalog.libraries.fontconfig.plainExplan: Fontconfig adds font discovery, and people choose it because FFmpeg can find installed fonts more reliably.
catalog.libraries.fontconfig.technicalEx: Check this when subtitle/text rendering should find installed fonts by name. It is not default because it is only useful with font-rendering workflows.
catalog.libraries.freetype.plainExplanat: FreeType adds font rendering, and people choose it because subtitles and drawn text need real font support.
catalog.libraries.freetype.reviewNote: Adds font rendering for subtitles and text filters.
catalog.libraries.freetype.technicalExpl: Check this when you need text drawing, subtitles, or filters that render fonts. It is not default because pure audio/video conversion may not render text.
catalog.libraries.frei0r.plainExplanatio: Frei0r adds extra video effect plugins, and people choose it when they want more creative filter choices. (Makes the build GPL.)
catalog.libraries.frei0r.reviewNote: Adds frei0r video effects. GPL effect.
catalog.libraries.frei0r.technicalExplan: Check this when you need frei0r video effects filters. It is not default because these effects are optional creative filters and the dependency changes the resulting build to GPL.
catalog.libraries.fribidi.plainExplanati: FriBidi adds right-to-left text support, and people choose it because languages such as Arabic and Hebrew need correct text direction.
catalog.libraries.fribidi.technicalExpla: Check this when you need correct right-to-left or bidirectional text rendering. It is not default because it is only needed for languages/scripts that require bidi handling.
catalog.libraries.gme.plainExplanation: Game Music Emu adds old game music support, and people choose it to read music formats from classic game systems.
catalog.libraries.gme.reviewNote: Adds support for game music formats such as NSF, SPC, GYM, and other chiptune files.
catalog.libraries.gme.technicalExplanati: Check this when you need to read game music formats such as NSF, SPC, GYM, or other chiptune files. It is not default because game music formats are a niche use case.
catalog.libraries.gnutls.plainExplanatio: GnuTLS adds encrypted network support (TLS/SSL), and people choose it when they prefer the GnuTLS security library instead of OpenSSL.
catalog.libraries.gnutls.reviewNote: Adds HTTPS/TLS network support through GnuTLS. Choose this instead of OpenSSL when you want TLS support without OpenSSL's redistribution concerns.
catalog.libraries.gnutls.technicalExplan: Check this when FFmpeg must use HTTPS/TLS through GnuTLS. Do not select it together with OpenSSL: FFmpeg's configure script rejects both TLS backends at the same time. It is not default because local file conversion does not need network TLS support.
catalog.libraries.gsm.plainExplanation: GSM adds old phone-speech audio support, and people usually choose it for legacy voice files.
catalog.libraries.gsm.technicalExplanati: Check this when you need GSM audio compatibility for old telephony files. It is not default because GSM is a legacy/specialized codec.
catalog.libraries.harfbuzz.plainExplanat: HarfBuzz adds text shaping, and people choose it because complex scripts and mixed text need correct letter placement.
catalog.libraries.harfbuzz.technicalExpl: Check this when you need high-quality shaping for complex scripts in subtitles or drawn text. It is not default because basic Latin text does not need it.
catalog.libraries.ilbc.plainExplanation: iLBC adds internet speech audio support, and people usually choose it for some older voice-call recordings.
catalog.libraries.ilbc.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need iLBC speech codec compatibility. It is not default because iLBC is a specialized voice codec.
catalog.libraries.ladspa.plainExplanatio: LADSPA adds audio plugin support, and people choose it when they already have LADSPA effect plugins they want FFmpeg to use.
catalog.libraries.ladspa.reviewNote: Adds hosting of LADSPA audio plugins through the ladspa filter.
catalog.libraries.ladspa.technicalExplan: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.lc3.plainExplanation: LC3 adds low-complexity audio support, and people usually choose it for newer communication-style audio workflows.
catalog.libraries.lc3.reviewNote: Adds Low Complexity Communication Codec (LC3) audio support used by Bluetooth LE Audio.
catalog.libraries.lc3.technicalExplanati: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.lcms2.plainExplanation: Little CMS 2 adds color management, and people choose it because it helps preserve accurate colors during conversion.
catalog.libraries.lcms2.reviewNote: Adds ICC color-management support for accurate color handling.
catalog.libraries.lcms2.technicalExplana: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.lensfun.plainExplanati: lensfun adds lens correction, and people choose it to reduce camera-lens problems such as distortion or dark corners.
catalog.libraries.lensfun.reviewNote: Hidden from presets and the UI. If an old/manual configuration enables it, the backend checks whether the installed lensfun exposes the API used by this FFmpeg source and skips it with a warning if incompatible.
catalog.libraries.lensfun.technicalExpla: Future-compatibility backend only. Current MSYS2 lensfun exposes an older API than the FFmpeg lensfun filter source expects, so this option is not exposed in the UI. The backend keeps a guarded compatibility path for later versions.
catalog.libraries.libavcodec.plainExplan: FFmpeg's built-in codec library for encoding and decoding media.
catalog.libraries.libavcodec.reviewNote: FFmpeg's built-in codec library for encoding and decoding media.
catalog.libraries.libavcodec.technicalEx: This is one of FFmpeg's own libraries. Native decoders and encoders are enabled by default; external-library codecs still require explicit --enable-lib... flags.
catalog.libraries.libavfilter.plainExpla: FFmpeg's built-in filtering library for scaling, trimming, overlaying, subtitles, audio filters, and more.
catalog.libraries.libavfilter.reviewNote: FFmpeg's built-in filtering library for scaling, trimming, overlaying, subtitles, audio filters, and more.
catalog.libraries.libavfilter.technicalE: This is one of FFmpeg's own libraries. Some filters can become more capable when external libraries are selected.
catalog.libraries.libavformat.plainExpla: FFmpeg's built-in library for reading and writing media containers such as MP4, MOV, MKV, and WAV.
catalog.libraries.libavformat.reviewNote: FFmpeg's built-in library for reading and writing media containers such as MP4, MOV, MKV, and WAV.
catalog.libraries.libavformat.technicalE: This is one of FFmpeg's own libraries and does not require an external MSYS2 package.
catalog.libraries.libavutil.plainExplana: Shared utility code used by the rest of FFmpeg.
catalog.libraries.libavutil.reviewNote: Shared utility code used by the rest of FFmpeg.
catalog.libraries.libavutil.technicalExp: This is one of FFmpeg's own libraries and is required by normal FFmpeg builds.
catalog.libraries.libjxl.plainExplanatio: JPEG XL support adds JPEG XL image reading and writing, and people choose it for modern high-quality image compression.
catalog.libraries.libjxl.technicalExplan: Check this when you need JPEG XL image support. It is not default because JPEG XL is not needed for common video workflows and requires an external image codec package.
catalog.libraries.libplacebo.plainExplan: libplacebo adds advanced graphics-card video processing (GPU processing), and people choose it for high-quality scaling, color conversion, and tone mapping.
catalog.libraries.libplacebo.technicalEx: Check this when you need advanced GPU-style video rendering, HDR tone mapping, or shader-based processing. It is not default because it is specialized and adds a graphics-processing dependency.
catalog.libraries.libswresample.plainExp: Built-in audio resampling and sample-format conversion.
catalog.libraries.libswresample.reviewNo: Built-in audio resampling and sample-format conversion.
catalog.libraries.libswresample.technica: This is one of FFmpeg's own libraries and does not require an external package.
catalog.libraries.libswscale.plainExplan: Built-in image scaling and pixel-format conversion.
catalog.libraries.libswscale.reviewNote: Built-in image scaling and pixel-format conversion.
catalog.libraries.libswscale.technicalEx: This is one of FFmpeg's own libraries and does not require an external package.
catalog.libraries.libvpx.plainExplanatio: libvpx adds VP8 and VP9 video encoding, and people often choose it because it works well for WebM video used on the web.
catalog.libraries.libvpx.reviewNote: Adds VP8/VP9 support for WebM files.
catalog.libraries.libvpx.technicalExplan: Check this when you need WebM VP8/VP9 encoding or libvpx-specific behavior. It is not default because it adds an external codec package; ordinary MP4 workflows do not need it.
catalog.libraries.lv2.plainExplanation: LV2 adds audio plugin support, and people choose it when they need more advanced plugin-based audio effects.
catalog.libraries.lv2.reviewNote: Adds hosting of LV2 audio plugins through the lv2 filter.
catalog.libraries.lv2.technicalExplanati: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.modplug.plainExplanati: libmodplug adds older module music input, and people choose it for compatibility with old tracker music formats.
catalog.libraries.modplug.technicalExpla: Check this when you need tracker/module audio formats such as MOD/XM/S3M. It is not default because those formats are niche.
catalog.libraries.mp3lame.plainExplanati: LAME adds MP3 audio encoding, and people choose it because MP3 plays almost everywhere.
catalog.libraries.mp3lame.technicalExpla: Check this when you need reliable MP3 encoding. It is not default because MP3 output is only needed for audio export workflows and adds an external encoder package.
catalog.libraries.mysofa.plainExplanatio: libmysofa adds spatial audio data support, and people choose it when headphone-style 3D audio filtering is needed.
catalog.libraries.mysofa.reviewNote: Adds SOFA HRTF loading for the sofalizer binaural spatial-audio filter.
catalog.libraries.mysofa.technicalExplan: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.native-codecs.plainExp: FFmpeg includes many native decoders and encoders before you add external codec libraries.
catalog.libraries.native-codecs.reviewNo: FFmpeg includes many native decoders and encoders before you add external codec libraries.
catalog.libraries.native-codecs.technica: Native FFmpeg decoders and encoders are enabled in a normal source build. External codec libraries are separate choices and use their own --enable-lib... flags.
catalog.libraries.native-formats.plainEx: FFmpeg includes many built-in readers and writers for media containers.
catalog.libraries.native-formats.reviewN: FFmpeg includes many built-in readers and writers for media containers.
catalog.libraries.native-formats.technic: These are part of FFmpeg itself. External libraries can add support or improve specific formats, but the base format layer is not an external package.
catalog.libraries.nvenc.plainExplanation: NVENC adds NVIDIA graphics-card encoding (GPU encoding), and people choose it because it makes video encoding much faster on NVIDIA systems.
catalog.libraries.nvenc.reviewNote: Enables NVIDIA GPU video encoding (h264_nvenc, hevc_nvenc, av1_nvenc) and CUVID decoding. NVIDIA libraries load at runtime from the driver; the build stays LGPL. Requires a compatible NVIDIA GPU and driver.
catalog.libraries.nvenc.technicalExplana: Check this when you need NVIDIA GPU-accelerated video encoding (h264_nvenc, hevc_nvenc, av1_nvenc) or CUVID hardware decoding. It is not default because it requires a compatible NVIDIA GPU and driver.
catalog.libraries.oapv.plainExplanation: OAPV adds APV video encoding (Advanced Professional Video), and people usually choose it for specialized professional video workflows.
catalog.libraries.oapv.reviewNote: Adds AP Video (APV) professional intraframe codec support through liboapv.
catalog.libraries.oapv.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need AP Video (APV) professional intraframe codec support. It is not default because APV is a new, specialized format aimed at high-quality production workflows rather than ordinary delivery.
catalog.libraries.openal.plainExplanatio: OpenAL adds audio device support, and people choose it when they need extra audio capture or playback device options.
catalog.libraries.openal.technicalExplan: Check this when you need OpenAL audio input. It is not default because it is a device/input feature, not needed for normal file conversion.
catalog.libraries.opencl.plainExplanatio: OpenCL adds graphics-card processing (GPU compute), and people choose it when supported filters can run faster on the graphics card.
catalog.libraries.opencl.reviewNote: Adds OpenCL GPU acceleration for filters that support it. Requires an OpenCL runtime from your GPU driver.
catalog.libraries.opencl.technicalExplan: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.opencore-amr.plainExpl: OpenCORE AMR adds AMR speech audio support, and people choose it to read older phone or voice-recording files.
catalog.libraries.opencore-amr.reviewNot: Adds AMR-NB and AMR-WB decoding support for mobile-phone voice recordings. This requires FFmpeg's version-3 license switch.
catalog.libraries.opencore-amr.technical: Check this when you need AMR-NB or AMR-WB support for phone/voice recordings. It is not default because AMR is a specialized mobile/telephony format, and FFmpeg requires --enable-version3 for this library.
catalog.libraries.openh264.plainExplanat: OpenH264 adds H.264 video encoding, and people often choose it when they need a simpler H.264 option with a different license profile than x264.
catalog.libraries.openh264.technicalExpl: Check this when you specifically need Cisco OpenH264 behavior or compatibility. It is not default because x264 is usually the preferred H.264 encoder when GPL is acceptable, and native FFmpeg already covers many H.264 tasks.
catalog.libraries.openjpeg.plainExplanat: OpenJPEG adds JPEG 2000 image support, and people choose it for archive, cinema, or professional image workflows.
catalog.libraries.openjpeg.technicalExpl: Check this when you need JPEG 2000 files, often used in cinema, archive, or medical/media workflows. It is not default because JPEG 2000 is not common for ordinary video conversion.
catalog.libraries.openmpt.plainExplanati: OpenMPT adds module music input (tracker music), and people choose it to read old or scene-style music files.
catalog.libraries.openmpt.reviewNote: Adds modern tracker/module audio support (MOD, XM, S3M, IT, and others). More actively maintained than libmodplug.
catalog.libraries.openmpt.technicalExpla: Check this when you need to play tracker/module audio files (MOD, XM, S3M, IT). Prefer this over libmodplug for newer files. It is not default because module audio is a niche format.
catalog.libraries.openssl.plainExplanati: OpenSSL adds encrypted network support (TLS/SSL), and people choose it because it enables HTTPS and other secure media connections. (Makes the build nonfree.)
catalog.libraries.openssl.reviewNote: Adds HTTPS/TLS network support through OpenSSL. Choose this instead of GnuTLS when you specifically need OpenSSL-compatible TLS behavior.
catalog.libraries.openssl.technicalExpla: Check this when FFmpeg must use HTTPS/TLS through OpenSSL. Do not select it together with GnuTLS: FFmpeg's configure script rejects both TLS backends at the same time. It is not default because it can make redistribution more sensitive and many local conversions do not need network TLS.
catalog.libraries.opus.plainExplanation: Opus adds modern audio encoding, and people choose it because it gives high quality at small file sizes for speech, music, and streaming.
catalog.libraries.opus.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need Opus audio for WebM, streaming, voice, or low-bitrate audio. It is not default because it adds an external codec package; simple AAC/MP3-style workflows may not need it.
catalog.libraries.png.plainExplanation: PNG support improves PNG image handling, and people choose it when they need reliable lossless still-image input or output.
catalog.libraries.png.reviewNote: PNG support is usually native; this installs libpng for filters/tools that need it.
catalog.libraries.png.technicalExplanati: Check this only when you need libpng for related tools or filters. It is not default because basic PNG image handling is commonly available through FFmpeg's native code.
catalog.libraries.qrencode.plainExplanat: qrencode adds QR code generation, and people choose it when they need to create QR codes inside images or video.
catalog.libraries.qrencode.reviewNote: Adds QR code generation for the qrencode source filter.
catalog.libraries.qrencode.technicalExpl: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.qsv.plainExplanation: Quick Sync Video adds Intel hardware encoding (GPU media engine), and people choose it because many Intel systems can encode video quickly with low CPU use.
catalog.libraries.qsv.reviewNote: Enables Intel Quick Sync hardware encoding and decoding (h264_qsv, hevc_qsv, av1_qsv, vp9_qsv). Requires an Intel GPU with Quick Sync support and the Intel oneVPL runtime.
catalog.libraries.qsv.technicalExplanati: Check this when you need Intel Quick Sync hardware encoding or decoding (h264_qsv, hevc_qsv, av1_qsv, vp9_qsv). It is not default because it requires an Intel GPU with Quick Sync support and the Intel oneVPL runtime installed.
catalog.libraries.rav1e.plainExplanation: rav1e adds AV1 video encoding, and people often choose it when they want another AV1 encoder for comparing speed and quality.
catalog.libraries.rav1e.technicalExplana: Check this when you specifically want the rav1e AV1 encoder. It is not default because it is a specialized AV1 encoder and most users do not need multiple AV1 encoders.
catalog.libraries.rist.plainExplanation: librist adds reliable stream transport, and people choose it for professional streaming over unstable networks.
catalog.libraries.rist.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need RIST broadcast/streaming transport. It is not default because it is a specialized live-video transport.
catalog.libraries.rsvg.plainExplanation: librsvg adds SVG rendering (vector image rendering), and people choose it to turn scalable graphic files into normal images or video frames.
catalog.libraries.rsvg.reviewNote: Adds SVG rasterization so vector overlays and images can be rendered.
catalog.libraries.rsvg.technicalExplanat: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.rtmp.plainExplanation: librtmp adds RTMP streaming, and people choose it for compatibility with older live-streaming servers.
catalog.libraries.rtmp.reviewNote: Adds RTMP/RTMPE streaming through librtmp instead of FFmpeg's native RTMP.
catalog.libraries.rtmp.technicalExplanat: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.rubberband.plainExplan: Rubber Band adds tempo and pitch changing, and people choose it because it can change speed or pitch with better sound quality. (Makes the build GPL.)
catalog.libraries.rubberband.reviewNote: Adds high quality audio time-stretching/pitch-shifting. GPL effect.
catalog.libraries.rubberband.technicalEx: Check this when you need high-quality audio time-stretching or pitch shifting. It is not default because it is only needed for special audio processing and changes the resulting build to GPL.
catalog.libraries.sdl2.plainExplanation: SDL2 adds simple media output support, and people choose it when an FFmpeg workflow needs preview or playback output.
catalog.libraries.sdl2.reviewNote: Adds SDL2 support, mainly useful for ffplay.
catalog.libraries.sdl2.technicalExplanat: Check this when you want ffplay or SDL-based playback support. It is not default because this builder is mainly for ffmpeg/ffprobe workflows, and playback UI support adds a separate dependency.
catalog.libraries.shaderc.plainExplanati: shaderc adds shader compilation (GPU effect code), and people choose it when advanced graphics-card filters need shader support.
catalog.libraries.shaderc.reviewNote: Adds runtime Vulkan shader compilation used by GPU filters such as libplacebo.
catalog.libraries.shaderc.technicalExpla: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.shine.plainExplanation: Shine adds simple fixed-point MP3 encoding, and people usually choose it only for special low-power or compatibility cases.
catalog.libraries.shine.reviewNote: Adds a fast fixed-point MP3 encoder, useful where floating-point speed is limited.
catalog.libraries.shine.technicalExplana: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.snappy.plainExplanatio: Snappy adds fast data compression support, and people choose it when a file format requires Snappy compatibility.
catalog.libraries.snappy.reviewNote: Adds Snappy compression used by the HAP GPU video codec.
catalog.libraries.snappy.technicalExplan: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.soxr.plainExplanation: SoX Resampler adds high-quality sample-rate conversion (audio rate conversion), and people choose it because it keeps audio cleaner when changing sample rates.
catalog.libraries.soxr.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need very high-quality audio resampling. It is not default because FFmpeg can resample audio without it, and many users do not need the extra quality/speed tradeoff.
catalog.libraries.speex.plainExplanation: Speex adds speech-focused audio support, and people usually choose it for older voice recordings or compatibility.
catalog.libraries.speex.technicalExplana: Check this when you need the older Speex speech codec. It is not default because Opus is usually preferred for modern speech/audio workflows.
catalog.libraries.srt.plainExplanation: SRT adds reliable live streaming, and people choose it because it can keep streams more stable on unreliable networks.
catalog.libraries.srt.reviewNote: Adds Secure Reliable Transport protocol support.
catalog.libraries.srt.technicalExplanati: Check this when you need Secure Reliable Transport streaming. It is not default because SRT is for live/remote streaming workflows, not ordinary local conversion.
catalog.libraries.ssh.plainExplanation: libssh adds secure remote file access, and people choose it to read or write media through SSH or SFTP servers.
catalog.libraries.ssh.technicalExplanati: Check this when FFmpeg must read or write through SSH/SFTP-style protocols. It is not default because most users use local files or HTTPS instead.
catalog.libraries.svt-av1.plainExplanati: SVT-AV1 adds AV1 video encoding, and people often choose it because it gives modern compression with practical encoding speed.
catalog.libraries.svt-av1.technicalExpla: Check this when you need faster AV1 encoding than libaom on modern CPUs. It is not default because it adds a large external encoder and is unnecessary unless you are creating AV1 video.
catalog.libraries.svtjpegxs.plainExplana: SVT JPEG XS adds JPEG XS encoding, and people usually choose it for low-delay professional media workflows.
catalog.libraries.svtjpegxs.reviewNote: Hidden from presets and the UI. If an old/manual configuration enables it, the backend tries the MSYS2 package first, then the official upstream source, and skips this feature with a warning if neither is compatible.
catalog.libraries.svtjpegxs.technicalExp: Future-compatibility backend only. Current packaged/repository states may not satisfy FFmpeg's SvtJpegxs requirement, so this option is not exposed in the UI. The backend keeps a guarded fallback path for later compatibility.
catalog.libraries.tesseract.plainExplana: Tesseract adds OCR text recognition (reading letters from images), and people choose it to extract visible text from images or video frames.
catalog.libraries.tesseract.reviewNote: Adds OCR filter support through Tesseract.
catalog.libraries.tesseract.technicalExp: Check this when you need OCR from video/images. It is not default because OCR is a heavy, specialized feature and requires extra language data for useful results.
catalog.libraries.theora.plainExplanatio: Theora adds Ogg Theora video encoding, and people usually choose it when they need support for an older open video format.
catalog.libraries.theora.reviewNote: Adds Ogg Theora video encoding and decoding.
catalog.libraries.theora.technicalExplan: Check this when you need Ogg Theora video support for OGG containers. It is not default because Theora is an older format with limited modern use.
catalog.libraries.twolame.plainExplanati: TwoLAME adds MP2 audio encoding, and people choose it for broadcast, DVD, or older media workflows that need MP2.
catalog.libraries.twolame.technicalExpla: Check this when you need MP2 audio encoding for broadcast or legacy workflows. It is not default because MP2 is uncommon for ordinary users.
catalog.libraries.vidstab.plainExplanati: vidstab adds video stabilization, and people choose it because it can reduce camera shake and make footage look smoother.
catalog.libraries.vidstab.technicalExpla: Check this when you need video stabilization filters to remove camera shake. It is not default because it is a specialized post-processing feature.
catalog.libraries.vmaf.plainExplanation: VMAF adds video quality measurement, and people choose it because it gives a useful score for comparing an encoded video with the original.
catalog.libraries.vmaf.reviewNote: Adds Netflix VMAF video quality measurement filters.
catalog.libraries.vmaf.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need objective video quality scoring with VMAF. It is not default because it is for testing/comparison workflows, not normal playback or conversion.
catalog.libraries.vo-amrwbenc.plainExpla: VisualOn AMR-WB adds AMR-WB speech encoding, and people choose it when they need wideband mobile-style voice audio.
catalog.libraries.vo-amrwbenc.reviewNote: Adds AMR-WB encoding support for narrow telephony workflows. This requires FFmpeg's version-3 license switch.
catalog.libraries.vo-amrwbenc.technicalE: Check this when you need AMR-WB encoding for narrow telephony workflows. It is not default because the format is specialized, and FFmpeg requires --enable-version3 for this library.
catalog.libraries.vorbis.plainExplanatio: Vorbis adds Ogg Vorbis audio encoding, and people choose it when they want an open audio format with good quality.
catalog.libraries.vorbis.technicalExplan: Check this when you need Vorbis audio, usually for Ogg/WebM-style workflows. It is not default because Vorbis is less common in ordinary MP4 workflows.
catalog.libraries.vvenc.plainExplanation:
VVenc adds VVC/H.266 video encoding, and people usually choose it to test very new compression technology with limited playback support.
**No MSYS2 package exists, so the build fails unless you build and install vvenc into the MSYS2 prefix yourself.**
catalog.libraries.vvenc.reviewNote:
Adds Versatile Video Coding (VVC/H.266) encoding.
**No prebuilt MSYS2 package exists**, so you must build and install vvenc into the selected MSYS2 prefix yourself or FFmpeg configure will fail for this library.
catalog.libraries.vvenc.technicalExplana: Check this when you need VVC/H.266 encoding. It is not default because VVC is an emerging codec with very limited decoder support outside research tools, and MSYS2 ships no prebuilt vvenc package — you must provide the library yourself or the build will fail at FFmpeg configure.
catalog.libraries.webp.plainExplanation: WebP support adds WebP image reading and writing, and people choose it because WebP is common on websites.
catalog.libraries.webp.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need to read or write WebP images or animated WebP. It is not default because normal video workflows usually use video containers rather than WebP.
catalog.libraries.whisper.plainExplanati: whisper.cpp adds speech recognition, and people choose it to turn spoken audio into text.
catalog.libraries.whisper.reviewNote: Adds the whisper speech-to-text filter for generating transcripts from audio.
catalog.libraries.whisper.technicalExpla: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.x264.plainExplanation: x264 adds H.264 video encoding, and people often choose it because it gives very wide playback compatibility with reliable quality. (Makes the build GPL.)
catalog.libraries.x264.reviewNote: Adds H.264 encoding. Good compatibility, but it changes the build to GPL.
catalog.libraries.x264.technicalExplanat: Most users can already decode H.264 with FFmpeg's native code. Check this only when you need to encode H.264 with the widely compatible x264 encoder. It is not default because it changes the resulting build to GPL.
catalog.libraries.x265.plainExplanation: x265 adds H.265 video encoding, and people often choose it because it can make smaller files than H.264 while keeping good visual quality. (Makes the build GPL.)
catalog.libraries.x265.reviewNote: Adds HEVC/H.265 encoding. Smaller files than H.264, but GPL.
catalog.libraries.x265.technicalExplanat: Most users can already handle many HEVC files with FFmpeg's native code. Check this when you need x265 HEVC encoding for smaller files at slower encode speed. It is not default because it changes the resulting build to GPL.
catalog.libraries.xavs2.plainExplanation:
xAVS2 adds AVS2 video encoding, and people usually choose it for media workflows that need this regional video standard. (Makes the build GPL.)
**No MSYS2 package exists, so the build fails unless you build and install xavs2 into the MSYS2 prefix yourself.**
catalog.libraries.xavs2.reviewNote:
Adds AVS2 video encoding. GPL effect.
**No prebuilt MSYS2 package exists**, so you must build and install xavs2 into the selected MSYS2 prefix yourself or FFmpeg configure will fail for this library.
catalog.libraries.xavs2.technicalExplana: Check this when you need AVS2 video encoding. It is not default because AVS2 is uncommon outside specific regional or archival workflows, it changes the resulting build to GPL, and MSYS2 ships no prebuilt xavs2 package — you must provide the library yourself or the build will fail at FFmpeg configure.
catalog.libraries.xevd.plainExplanation: XEVD adds EVC video decoding (Essential Video Coding), and people usually choose it when they need to read this newer video format.
catalog.libraries.xevd.reviewNote: Adds Essential Video Coding (EVC) decoding through xevd.
catalog.libraries.xevd.technicalExplanat: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it adds another external package to the build.
catalog.libraries.xeve.plainExplanation: XEVE adds EVC video encoding (Essential Video Coding), and people usually choose it for testing a newer video standard.
catalog.libraries.xeve.reviewNote: Adds Essential Video Coding (EVC) encoding for broadcast and research workflows.
catalog.libraries.xeve.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need EVC encoding for broadcast or research. It is not default because EVC is only used in specialized workflows.
catalog.libraries.xml2.plainExplanation: libxml2 adds XML support (structured text data), and people choose it when formats or features need XML parsing.
catalog.libraries.xml2.reviewNote: Adds XML parsing support used by some formats/protocols.
catalog.libraries.xml2.technicalExplanat: Check this when a format, manifest, or protocol needs XML parsing. It is not default because common local conversion usually does not need XML support.
catalog.libraries.xvid.plainExplanation: Xvid adds older MPEG-4 Part 2 video encoding, and people usually choose it only for compatibility with old players or devices. (Makes the build GPL.)
catalog.libraries.xvid.reviewNote: Adds Xvid MPEG-4 Part 2 video encoding. GPL effect.
catalog.libraries.xvid.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need Xvid MPEG-4 Part 2 encoding for compatibility with older devices or workflows. It is not default because MPEG-4 Part 2 has been largely superseded by H.264, and it changes the resulting build to GPL.
catalog.libraries.zimg.plainExplanation: zimg improves resizing and color conversion, and people choose it because it gives cleaner scaling and better color handling.
catalog.libraries.zimg.reviewNote: Adds high-quality resizing, colorspace, and bit-depth conversion filters.
catalog.libraries.zimg.technicalExplanat: Check this when you need high-quality resizing, color conversion, or bit-depth conversion. It is not default because normal scaling works without it, while zimg adds a specialized processing dependency.
catalog.libraries.zmq.plainExplanation: ZeroMQ adds message-based control, and people choose it to control some FFmpeg workflows while they are running.
catalog.libraries.zmq.technicalExplanati: Check this when you need ZeroMQ filter/control messaging. It is not default because it is for automation/control workflows rather than normal conversion.
catalog.libraries.zvbi.plainExplanation: libzvbi adds teletext and VBI support (hidden broadcast text data), and people choose it to extract text or subtitles from older broadcasts. (Makes the build GPL.)
catalog.libraries.zvbi.reviewNote: Adds teletext decoding from DVB/analog VBI data. GPL effect.
catalog.libraries.zvbi.technicalExplanat: Check this only when you need this specific feature. It is not default because it changes the resulting FFmpeg build to GPL.
catalog.options.default-ffmpeg.plainExpl: Builds the main command-line converter most users run.
catalog.options.default-ffmpeg.technical: Checked because ffmpeg.exe is part of a normal program build.
catalog.options.default-ffprobe.plainExp: Builds the media inspection tool used to read stream and container information.
catalog.options.default-ffprobe.technica: Checked because ffprobe.exe is part of a normal program build.
catalog.options.default-programs.plainEx: FFmpeg normally builds command-line programs such as ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe.
catalog.options.default-programs.technic: Checked because programs are built in a normal source build. Disable only if you want libraries without command-line tools.
catalog.options.default-static.plainExpl: FFmpeg normally builds static libraries from source.
catalog.options.default-static.technical: Checked because this is normal FFmpeg configure behavior. No extra flag is needed unless you choose a different output type.
catalog.options.disable-asm.plainExplana:
Uses slower but simpler C code paths if assembly causes build problems.
**<red>Risk</red>: this removes nearly all SIMD optimization, so encoding and decoding can be several times slower. Use it only when assembly actually breaks the build.**
catalog.options.disable-asm.technicalNot: Normally leave unchecked because FFmpeg is faster with assembly optimizations.
catalog.options.disable-autodetect.displ: Do not auto-use hidden system libraries
catalog.options.disable-autodetect.plain: Makes the build less surprising by using only explicitly selected external libraries.
catalog.options.disable-autodetect.techn: Good for transparent/reproducible builds. Select this when you want the Review page to explain every external dependency.
catalog.options.disable-debug.plainExpla: Makes normal-use output smaller and simpler.
catalog.options.disable-debug.technicalN: Not a normal source default. Select this for ordinary release-style local builds; leave unchecked when investigating build or runtime problems.
catalog.options.disable-doc.plainExplana: Makes the build smaller by not building local documentation files.
catalog.options.disable-doc.technicalNot: Not a normal source default. Select this when you only need binaries/libraries and do not need generated docs.
catalog.options.disable-ffplay.plainExpl: Skips the simple playback test program.
catalog.options.disable-ffplay.technical: Useful when SDL playback support is unnecessary. ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe are unaffected.
catalog.options.disable-stripping.plainE: Keeps more build information for debugging.
catalog.options.disable-stripping.techni: Usually unnecessary for ordinary users, but useful when diagnosing crashes or build problems.
catalog.options.disable-x86asm.plainExpl: Try this when NASM/YASM-related build problems occur.
catalog.options.enable-shared.plainExpla:
Creates DLL-style FFmpeg libraries for other programs to load.
**<red>Risk</red>: this switches the output to DLLs and turns off static builds, which often breaks linking against the static external libraries this tool installs — the build can fail, or produce an ffmpeg.exe that needs extra DLLs at run time.**
catalog.options.enable-shared.technicalN: FFmpeg platform documentation describes --enable-shared as the way to build FFmpeg libraries as DLLs on Windows. This changes the output type, so it is not selected by default here.
catalog.options.enable-small.plainExplan: Asks FFmpeg to prefer smaller output files over speed.
catalog.options.enable-small.technicalNo: Useful for constrained environments; may reduce performance.
catalog.options.enable-lto.plainExplanat: Lets the compiler optimize across files for a smaller and sometimes faster binary.
catalog.options.enable-lto.technicalNote: Increases build time and memory use. Leave unchecked if linking fails or runs out of memory.
catalog.options.enable-runtime-cpudetect: Detect CPU features at run time
Builds one binary that picks CPU optimizations while running, so it works across different processors.
Useful when sharing the build with other machines. Slightly slower than a build tuned for one specific CPU.
catalog.options.pkg-config-static.plainE: Tells pkg-config to pull the full static dependency chain when linking external libraries.
catalog.options.pkg-config-static.techni: Often required for static Windows builds that use external libraries, so configure can find every transitive dependency. Has no effect on a shared/DLL build.
catalog.options.disable-network.plainExp: Builds FFmpeg without any network protocols for a smaller, offline-only tool.
catalog.options.disable-network.technica: Select for local-only conversion or hardened builds. Disables HTTP, HTTPS, RTMP, SRT, and every other network input/output, so streaming protocols stop working even if their libraries are selected.

plan.warnings.msys2ArchiveUrlEmpty: MSYS2 archive URL is empty. Use an official MSYS2 tar archive URL before approval. .tar.zst is recommended, and .tar.xz is accepted as a fallback.
plan.warnings.msys2ArchiveUrlNotTar: Use an MSYS2 tar archive URL here. The official .exe installer is valid MSYS2, but this app does not run installers; it verifies and extracts tar archives inside the selected workspace. Use .tar.zst when possible, or .tar.xz as a fallback. Put the matching .sig URL in the signature field.
plan.warnings.msys2ArchiveUrlBadExtensio: MSYS2 archive URL must end with .tar.zst or .tar.xz. This app uses tar archives so it can verify and extract files itself without running an installer.
plan.warnings.msys2SignatureMissing: No MSYS2 .sig URL was supplied. The app can calculate SHA-256, but signature verification is the better official authenticity check.
plan.warnings.msys2SignatureBadExtension: MSYS2 signature URL must end with .sig.
plan.warnings.msys2SignatureMismatch: MSYS2 signature URL does not exactly match the archive URL plus .sig. This may be intentional, but usually the signature URL should be the archive URL followed by .sig.
plan.warnings.msys2ShaBad: MSYS2 SHA-256 must be exactly 64 hexadecimal characters. If you pasted a .sig file, remove it; .sig is a signature file, not a hash.
plan.warnings.shellProfileBad: Windows shell profile must be ucrt64, mingw64, or clang64.
plan.warnings.ffmpegArchiveUrlEmpty: FFmpeg source archive URL is empty. Paste an official fixed release archive URL before approval.
plan.warnings.ffmpegSignatureMissing: FFmpeg source signature URL is empty. FFmpeg releases are verified through the matching .asc PGP signature.
plan.warnings.ffmpegSignatureBadExtensio: FFmpeg signature URL must end in .asc. Do not paste the PGP signature text; use the URL of the matching .asc file.
plan.warnings.ffmpegShaMissing: No FFmpeg SHA-256 was supplied. This is normal for the official release page: the app will verify the .asc PGP signature and calculate SHA-256 for the log.
plan.warnings.ffmpegShaBad: FFmpeg SHA-256 must be exactly 64 hexadecimal characters. If you have a .asc or .sig file, do not paste it into this field; it is a signature file, not a hash.
plan.warnings.parallelJobTooHigh: Parallel job count must not exceed 256.
plan.warnings.version3Added: FFmpeg version-3 license switch was added because a selected library requires --enable-version3.
plan.warnings.workspaceNotAbsolute: Workspace directory must be an absolute path.
plan.warnings.workspaceContainsSpace: Workspace path contains a space. Some FFmpeg dependency builds may fail with spaces in paths.
plan.warnings.tlsBackendConflict: Choose one TLS backend: OpenSSL or GnuTLS. FFmpeg cannot configure both --enable-openssl and --enable-gnutls at the same time.
plan.warnings.shaderCompilerConflict: Choose one runtime shader compiler: libshaderc or libglslang. FFmpeg configure rejects --enable-libshaderc and --enable-libglslang together; if in doubt, keep libshaderc and disable libglslang.
plan.warnings.networkDisabledWithProtoco: "Remove all networking support" is selected, so these selected network libraries will not work: {libraries}. Deselect "Remove all networking support" or remove those libraries.
plan.warnings.licenseBoundaryBad: Derived license boundary must be lgpl-local, gpl-local, or nonfree-local.
plan.warnings.licenseGpl: License boundary was set to GPL local because selected libraries or flags require --enable-gpl.
plan.warnings.licenseNonfree: License boundary was set to nonfree local because selected libraries or flags require --enable-nonfree. Do not redistribute this build unless you have reviewed the license obligations.
plan.warnings.libraryNoMsys2Package: No prebuilt MSYS2 package exists for {library} ({upstream}). FFmpeg configure will fail for this library unless you build and install {upstream} into the selected MSYS2 prefix yourself.

catalog.libraries.cairo.plainExplanation: Cairo adds 2D graphics rendering, and people choose it when filters need generated graphics, overlays, or drawn visual elements.
catalog.libraries.cairo.reviewNote: Adds 2D vector graphics rendering support for graphics-oriented filters.
catalog.libraries.cairo.technicalExplana: Choose this when you need FFmpeg features that render 2D vector graphics through Cairo. It is a graphics/filter support library, not a codec.
catalog.libraries.glslang.plainExplanati: glslang adds shader compilation (GPU effect code), and people choose it when a build specifically needs this shader toolchain.
catalog.libraries.glslang.reviewNote: Adds runtime GLSL/HLSL to SPIR-V shader compilation support.
catalog.libraries.glslang.technicalExpla: Choose this for shader-based processing paths that need runtime GLSL/HLSL to SPIR-V compilation, especially around Vulkan/GPU filter workflows.
catalog.libraries.opencv.plainExplanatio: OpenCV adds computer vision support (image analysis by code), and people choose it for experimental visual detection or image-processing workflows.
catalog.libraries.opencv.reviewNote: Adds OpenCV-backed video filtering and computer-vision processing support.
catalog.libraries.opencv.technicalExplan: Choose this only when you need OpenCV-backed FFmpeg filters or computer-vision processing. It is large and not required for ordinary encoding.
catalog.libraries.opencolorio.plainExpla: OpenColorIO adds professional color management, and people choose it for film, animation, and studio color workflows.
catalog.libraries.opencolorio.reviewNote: Adds OpenColorIO color-management and color-transform support.
catalog.libraries.opencolorio.technicalE: Choose this for professional color-management workflows, especially VFX, animation, and color-transform pipelines. It is not needed for ordinary format compatibility.
catalog.libraries.dvdread.plainExplanati: libdvdread adds DVD input support, and people choose it to inspect or convert DVD media. (Makes the build GPL.)
catalog.libraries.dvdread.reviewNote: Adds DVD-Video disc structure reading support.
catalog.libraries.dvdread.technicalExpla: Choose this when FFmpeg needs to read DVD-Video disc structures. DVD support is niche and may affect the license boundary depending on the rest of the build.
catalog.libraries.jack.plainExplanation: JACK adds professional audio routing support, and people choose it when FFmpeg must connect to a studio-style audio system.
catalog.libraries.jack.reviewNote: Adds JACK low-latency audio server input/output support.
catalog.libraries.jack.technicalExplanat: Choose this for live audio routing through the JACK audio server. It is useful for studio/live workflows, but not for ordinary file conversion on 윈도우.
catalog.libraries.pulse.plainExplanation: PulseAudio adds Linux audio-system support, and people choose it when FFmpeg must capture or output audio through PulseAudio.
catalog.libraries.pulse.reviewNote: Adds PulseAudio sound server input support.
catalog.libraries.pulse.technicalExplana: Choose this only when you need PulseAudio input support. It is available in MSYS2, but it is not a normal native 윈도우 audio backend.
catalog.libraries.rabbitmq.plainExplanat: RabbitMQ-C adds message-queue support, and people choose it for specialized automated media pipelines.
catalog.libraries.rabbitmq.technicalExpl: Choose this when FFmpeg must interact with RabbitMQ/AMQP messaging workflows. It is a specialized network/protocol feature, not a normal media-conversion option.
